theater: 尼羅河三角洲曼蘇拉城郊

battle.name: 達魯古城之戰
battle.theater: 尼羅河三角洲曼蘇拉城郊
battle.brief: 1115年1月，耶路撒冷王國王鮑德溫一世率數百騎士南下埃及，在佩盧西烏姆支流搭浮橋渡河，黎明奇襲維齊爾阿夫達勒設於曼蘇拉的法蒂瑪營地，攻破營地、奪其軍械輜重；繼而圍曼蘇拉城七日不下，進軍開羅又因援軍逼近而撤退。卡面配重投石車是同期成形的新式攻城機，本役未派上用場，全靠奇襲與渡河。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 達魯古城之戰是1115年1月耶路撒冷王國與法蒂瑪王朝在埃及尼羅河三角洲的一場遭遇戰，規模不大，卻是拉丁東方立國後第一次由國王親自率軍深入敵國腹地的遠征。交戰的一方是法蒂瑪王朝（法蒂瑪王朝於此際重掌埃及與敘利亞沿岸，首都開羅與新宮城曼蘇拉相距不過半日路程），另一方是1110年代前期剛在巴勒斯坦站穩腳跟的耶路撒冷王國。法蒂瑪方面由哈里發艾米爾坐鎮軍中，但全權指揮交給維齊爾阿夫達勒；軍隊由埃及本地步兵、阿拉伯與柏柏爾系輕騎、馬穆魯克奴隸騎兵組成，另有尼羅河上的船隊負責輸送糧秣、帳幕與攻城器材，後方以開羅與曼蘇拉的城防、倉儲與船塢作依托。耶路撒冷方面則是一支規模極小的遠征軍：由鮑德溫一世親領王國核心的封建騎士，配合耶路撒冷城內的步兵與雇傭兵，另有工匠、嚮導與隨軍僕役隨行，指揮體系極為簡單——國王本人在前線統兵，騎士按封邑與旗幟編隊，糧秣則靠就地徵發與劫奪維持，沒有任何攻城重器。兩軍無論在數量還是裝備層次上都極不對稱：一方是數百重騎配重步兵的精銳小隊，另一方是控制著尼羅河水路、兩座都城與廣闊三角洲的人海式大軍。
countriesEn: The Battle of Dar al-Mansurah was fought in January 1115 in the Nile delta of Egypt between the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem and the Fatimid Caliphate. It was a small engagement in numbers but the first time the new Latin state in the Levant sent a king personally with arms into the heart of the enemy's country. One side was the Fatimid dynasty, which had by then regained Egypt and the Syrian coast, and which ruled from Cairo and from the newer palace city of al-Mansurah, a mere half day's march apart. On the Fatimid side the caliph al-Amir was present with the army, but the command was vested in the vizier al-Afdal. The force was made up of Egyptian infantry, Arab and Berber light horse, the mamluk slave cavalry, and river craft that carried grain, tenting and siege material; the cities of Cairo and Mansurah and their stores and dockyards lay behind them. The other side was the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem: King Baldwin I himself led the core of the kingdom's feudal knights, with infantry and hired men from the city of Jerusalem, together with the craftsmen, guides and servants who moved with them. The command structure was minimal, the king in person at the head, knights grouped by fief and banner, supplies taken from the country as it advanced, and not a single heavy siege engine in the column. The two sides were grossly unequal in both numbers and equipment: a few hundred heavy cavalry with an equally small infantry on one hand, and on the other a mass army that held the river, two capitals and the whole delta.
people: 鮑德溫一世（Baldwin I of Jerusalem，約1050年至1118年）是本役的主導者。1110年從埃德蒙納伯爵之位奪得耶路撒冷王國的王位後，他於1113年還曾大敗艾梅爾的埃及援軍於阿爾蘇夫，1115年這次南征埃及則是他第一次主動把戰線推到地中海以外。軍中還有耶路撒冷王國的諸侯與本地陳羅的日耳曼系騎士，以及隨軍的教士、翻譯與嚮導，後者多為住在埃及的東方基督徒，負責引路、談判與採購糧食。法蒂瑪方面，哈里發艾米爾（al-Amir bi-A'llah，1102年至1130年在位）駐在新建的曼蘇拉宮城中，他的帳幕與印璽在奇襲中被法蘭克人奪去，人則退入開羅。真正負責戰局的是維齊爾阿夫達勒（al-Afdal），艾米爾的表兄、埃及的實際執政者，此役的指揮者；奇襲之後他主張放棄正面反擊，改以河海封鎖與襲擾來消耗法蘭克軍，後續的埃及防禦戰略基本依此展開。記錄此役的主要史家是阿拉伯編年史家伊本·阿西爾，其敘事見於《全史》（al-Kāmil fī al-Tārīkh），但他對法蒂瑪的敘述帶有阿拔斯派（法蒂瑪的世仇）難免的敵意；法蒂瑪方面的說法則見於後世史家伊本·伊德里斯與馬格里齊的追述。拉丁方面最重要的同期材料是《耶路撒冷史》（Historia Hierosolymitana）保存的鮑德溫致西方書信，信中同時提供兵力數字與求援的內容。
peopleEn: Baldwin I of Jerusalem (c. 1050–1118) was the man who drove this campaign. Having seized the kingship of Jerusalem in 1110 from the count of Edessa, he had already beaten al-Amir's Egyptian relief army at Ascalon in 1113; the descent into Egypt of 1115 was his first deliberate extension of the war beyond the Mediterranean shore. With him marched the barons of the kingdom and the local German-speaking knights, together with the clergy, interpreters and guides of the host, the latter mostly Eastern Christians resident in Egypt, who handled the roads, the negotiations and the purchase of food. On the Fatimid side the caliph al-Amir (al-Amir bi-A'llah, r. 1102–1130) was in the new palace city of Mansurah with the army; his tents and his seal were taken in the surprise, and he himself fell back into Cairo. The man actually responsible was the vizier al-Afdal, the caliph's cousin and Egypt's effective ruler, who commanded the field forces. After the surprise he argued against meeting the Franks in open battle and in favour of starving them out by river and sea interdiction and constant harrying, and that approach shaped the Egyptian defence for the rest of the war. The principal chronicler of the episode is the Arab historian Ibn al-Athir, whose account stands in the al-Kam'il fi al-Tarikh, though his narrative of the Fatimids carries the natural hostility of the Abbasids, hereditary enemies of the dynasty; the Fatimid side is known from later writers such as Ibn Idries and al-Maqrizi. The most important Latin contemporary source is the letter Baldwin sent to the West, preserved in the Historia Hierosolymitana, which supplies both the figures for his army and the substance of his appeal for aid.
kits: 本卡兵器是配重投石車（Trebuchet），即以長臂末端配重、用以把石彈拋過城牆的攻城機器。其技術源頭在東亞的拉索式投石車，經伊斯蘭世界的工程師改造，在十一世紀末至十二世紀初逐步過渡到以配重驅動的階段，義大利與黎凡特沿海的工匠正是在這段時間把它推向成熟。因此在1115年的埃及戰場上，配重投石車這一類器械正處在過渡地帶：法蒂瑪一方在開羅與曼蘇拉城頭常備的是大型拉索式投石車（manjaniq），能把石彈與燃燒的陶罐擲向城外的圍軍；法蘭克一方則連一台像樣的重型攻城機都沒有帶進埃及，直到1118年圍攻阿斯旺時才組織起河上封鎖與攻城器械的配合，而為這批人提供技術的正是比薩與熱那亞的航海與工程團體。本役真正大量投入的是輕武器與馬匹：法蘭克騎士的裝備是加鎖子甲、尖頭盔、圓盾或鳶盾、長矛與釘了圖釘的刺馬鎚，步兵以弩（arbalest）與手弩、方盾和投槍為主，馬匹是產於歐洲的沉重披甲戰馬；法蒂瑪的騎兵用複合弓與較輕的馬，步兵用短弓、長矛與小圓盾，軍中馬穆魯克騎兵作為衝鋒骨幹。營地方面需要大量繩索、木料、帳幕與旗幔，駱駝隊把糧食、箭矢與器材自尼羅河船隻搬上岸，這些帳幕、旗幔與軍械正是奇襲中被法蘭克人成批擄走的東西，而配重投石車在技術譜系上正是要取代這類依賴大量繩索木料與人力拖曳的早期投石機。
kitsEn: The card's weapon is the trebuchet, the counterweighted machine with a long arm that throws stones over a wall. Its ancestry lies in the East Asian traction trebuchet; worked on by engineers in the Islamic world, it was passing through the counterweight stage in the late eleventh and early twelfth centuries, and the shipwrights and engineers of Italy and the Levantine coast were the men who carried it to maturity. At the Egyptian battlefield of 1115 this class of machine was therefore in transition. The Fatimids kept large traction trebuchets (manjaniq) on the walls of Cairo and Mansurah, capable of hurling stones and burning jars at a besieger outside the walls; the Franks brought not one proper heavy engine into Egypt, and only in 1118, at the siege of Aswan, did they organise river interdiction together with siege material, and the Pisan and Genoese trading and engineering crews were the men who supplied that expertise. What was actually expended in large quantities here were light weapons and horses. The Frankish knight wore a mail coat, a pointed helm, a round or kite shield, and carried a lance and a spiked mace; his footmen used the arbalest and hand crossbows, kite and square shields, and javelins, and rode heavy destriers bred in Europe. Fatimid horse archers used composite bows on lighter mounts, their infantry carried short bows, spears and small round shields, and the mamluk cavalry formed the striking core of the army. On the logistics side, camps demanded enormous quantities of rope, timber, tenting and banners, and camel trains unloaded grain, arrows and equipment from the Nile boats. Those very tents, banners and weapons were what the Franks carried off in bulk after the surprise, and the trebuchet in the technical genealogy stands precisely for the machine meant to displace that early, rope-and-timber-and-manpower dependent artillery.
tactics: 鮑德溫這次遠征的全部戰術核心是速度、隱蔽與渡河。他避開沿海法蒂瑪據點密集與運河縱橫的地帶，取道南猶他與西奈東側的缺水荒漠，在一月至二月的季節裡急行穿越，隊伍極輕：騎兵與輕步兵為主，行軍縱隊與給養車隊分開，途中靠就地向遊牧部落與鄉村徵收糧水維繫。到達佩盧西烏姆支流（拉希德河汊）一帶時，遠征軍沒有強攻設防的渡口，而是用船隻搭成浮橋迅速渡過，避開了被攔阻的風險。奇襲安排在黎明前發動：鮑德溫把騎兵分置兩翼，步兵與隨軍僕役居中，突入時不與大營正面硬撞，而是直插營帳、器材堆與旗幔集中處，摧毀帳幕、擄走輜重與軍械，隨即在敵軍回神之前退出。法蒂瑪的應對則是典型的守方邏輯：維齊爾把大軍擺在開羅以西平坦的三角洲上，營地綿延，據說寬廣得一日行程都走不完，靠尼羅河的水路與城牆支撐；鮑德溫隨後進攻有護城河與城牆的曼蘇拉城，卻沒有能摧毀城防的重型器械，圍城七日不能下，法蒂瑪守軍又不斷出城反擊，鮑德溫只能解圍，轉而向開羅進逼，開羅外圍與部分城區隨即被放棄；得知上埃及方向有大軍逼近後，他立刻轉為撤退，帶著戰利品循原路穿越沙漠返回巴勒斯坦。整個戰役的勝負，幾乎全由渡河點的選擇與奇襲時機決定，而配重投石車那樣的器械在本役完全缺席。
tacticsEn: The whole tactical core of the expedition was speed, concealment and the crossing of the river. Baldwin avoided the coastal belt where the Fatimids' strongpoints and canals were dense, and took the arid track through southern Judaea and the eastern side of Sinai, pushing across it in the January–February season with a deliberately light column: horse and light infantry only, the marching column and the baggage train kept apart, and the host kept alive by taking grain and water from the desert settlements and camps on the march. On the Pelusium branch of the Nile, near Rashid, he did not force the defended crossing but went over it on a pontoon bridge made of boats, which removed the risk of being checked at the water. The surprise was launched before dawn. Baldwin placed horse on the two wings, infantry and servants in the centre, and instead of colliding with the front of the great camp the assault drove straight into the tents, the stacked equipment and the massed banners, tearing down the tenting, carrying off baggage and weapons, and then withdrawing before the enemy could recover. The Fatimid response followed the logic of the defender: the vizier drew up his army on the flat delta west of Cairo, in a camp so broad that it was said to take a full day's march to cross, resting on the Nile's water and on the city walls. Baldwin then turned against the walled and moated city of Mansurah, but without any heavy engine capable of breaching its defences; after seven days, and with the garrison sallying out to harry the besiegers, he had to lift the siege, and marched on Cairo, whose outer works were promptly abandoned. When he learned that a large army was approaching from Upper Egypt, he turned back at once and carried his plunder across the desert to Palestine. Almost every outcome in this campaign was decided by the choice of crossing and by the timing of the surprise, and the counterweight trebuchet was simply absent from the field.
data: 本役的日期大致可以確定在1115年1月25日黎明，戰役與隨後的埃及遠征延續到二月。兵力數字分歧很大：鮑德溫致西方的書信是拉丁方面最接近同期的一手材料，其中自述的騎士人數只是數百之譜，常被概括為約五百至七百名騎士，步兵與雜役約一千人；也有更保守的說法把全部作戰人員估在八百以下，說明這支遠征軍確實小得驚人。與此相對，法蒂瑪方面的野外部隊規模遠大於對手，各書形容其營地寬廣、帳幕旗幔與輜重數以千計，馬步軍總數當以萬計，但沒有留下可供核對的確數，因此較穩妥的說法是「以萬計的軍隊對數百名騎士」。圍城與行程的時間則有較清楚的記載：鮑德溫圍曼蘇拉城七日不能下，之後進軍開羅，因獲悉上埃及援軍接近而撤退，整段遠征在埃及境內停留約一個月；從耶路撒冷到曼蘇拉的直線距離不足三百公里，實際行程更長，撤退時穿越西奈的缺水地帶，史料記載隊伍因缺水與糧秣不足而大量掉隊，但沒有留下確切人數。損失的另一面是收穫：法蒂瑪的帳幕、旗幔、軍械、攻城器材與大量金銀財貨在奇襲中被成批擄走，這筆物資後來成為耶路撒冷王國的重要財源。作為對照，1118年鮑德溫再度進軍埃及圍攻阿斯旺，在那裡對峙約七個月後仍然無功而返；1121年的第三次遠征結果相仿，埃及線的戰役至此告一段落。
dataEn: The date of the action can be fixed with reasonable confidence to the dawn of 25 January 1115, and the campaign as a whole ran on into February. The figures for strength diverge sharply. Baldwin's letter to the West is the closest thing to a contemporary Latin primary source, and the number of knights he gives himself there is only several hundred, commonly summarised as somewhere between five hundred and seven hundred, with about a thousand foot soldiers and retainers; more conservative estimates put the whole fighting force below eight hundred, which shows how very small the expedition really was. On the Fatimid side the field army was far larger: the books describe the camp as very broad, with thousands of tents, banners and baggage, and the horse and foot in the tens of thousands, but no figure survives that can be checked, so the safer formulation is an army numbering in the tens of thousands against several hundred knights. The timing of the siege and the march is recorded more clearly. Baldwin lay before Mansurah seven days without taking it, then moved on Cairo, and turned back on hearing that a relief army was coming from Upper Egypt; the whole expedition spent about a month inside Egypt. The straight-line distance from Jerusalem to Mansurah is under three hundred kilometres, the marched route longer, and on the withdrawal across the waterless stretch of Sinai the chroniclers record heavy straggling for want of water and grain, though no reliable number of men is given. The other side of the account is the booty: tents, banners, weapons, siege equipment and a great quantity of treasure were carried off in bulk after the surprise, and that material later became a significant source of revenue for the kingdom of Jerusalem. For comparison, Baldwin's second Egyptian expedition of 1118 ended in the siege of Aswan, which lasted about seven months and also failed; the third expedition of 1121 ended in the same way, and the Egyptian front closed there.
cause: 達魯古城之戰的直接背景是法蒂瑪王朝與耶路撒冷王國在埃及與地中海東岸的長期拉鋸。法蒂瑪自1080年代末在埃及重新站穩腳跟後，把行政與宮廷中心從開羅遷到新建的曼蘇拉（1090年代初落成），並在阿爾蘇夫、提爾等沿海據點反覆進攻，試圖把法蘭克人的王國壓回地中海一隅。到1114年前後，戰線在耶路撒冷王國沿海的城市與港口一帶僵持不下，王國財政吃緊，沿海據點屢遭圍困，而法蒂瑪方面的財政與兵力遠在其上。鮑德溫面對的是一道算不過來的難題：以數百騎士對上以萬計的大軍，正面會戰必敗；但若龜縮防守，則沿海城鎮會被逐一消耗，人民與物資源源不斷流向開羅。於是他選擇了冒險的一條路：不等敵人來攻，直接插入三角洲，奪取對方的財富與士氣，把戰場推到法蒂瑪的家門口。同時，這次遠征也是一次向西方的求援行動——鮑德溫在信中描述自己以極少兵力打到開羅城下，請求西方派兵來救援耶路撒冷。有學者指出，法蒂瑪方面的遲緩反應同其維齊爾當時正把主要精力放在應付塞爾柱人於安納托利亞與伊拉克方向的壓力有關；法蒂瑪軍以為法蘭克人不敢穿越沙漠深入三角洲，因此對鮑德溫的推進估計不足，等到明白過來時營地已經被破。
causeEn: The immediate background to the Battle of Dar al-Mansurah was the long attritional contest between the Fatimid dynasty and the Kingdom of Jerusalem over Egypt and the eastern Mediterranean. After reasserting itself in Egypt in the late 1080s, the Fatimids had moved their administrative and court centre from Cairo to the newly built Mansurah in the early 1090s, and they struck repeatedly at the coastal strongpoints at Ascalon and Tyre in an attempt to press the Frankish kingdom back into a corner of the sea. By around 1114 the front had stalemated along the coast of the kingdom, its cities and ports were repeatedly invested, its finances were strained, and the Fatimids held an overwhelming superiority in men and money. Baldwin faced an arithmetical impossibility: several hundred knights could not win a set-piece battle against an army numbering in the tens of thousands, but a purely defensive posture meant losing the coastal cities one at a time and letting their wealth and stores flow steadily into Cairo. He therefore took the gamble of going in rather than waiting: striking into the delta to seize the enemy's treasure and confidence and to carry the war to the gates of the Fatimid capital. The expedition was at the same time an appeal to the West, for Baldwin's letter describes the small force with which he had struck to the gates of Cairo and asks for men to come to the aid of Jerusalem. Scholars have pointed out that the slowness of the Fatimid response was connected with the fact that the vizier's attention was fixed on the Seljuk pressure coming out of Anatolia and Iraq; the Fatimid army assumed that the Franks would not cross the desert and push deep into the delta, and it was not until the camp had been broken that they grasped what had happened.
impact: 這一役在拉丁與阿拉伯兩個世界都留下深痕。對耶路撒冷王國而言，鮑德溫以數百騎士打穿埃及、奪取法蒂瑪最高統帥的營帳與大批財貨，這一消息在歐洲引起強烈回響：他致西方的書信成為「耶路撒冷求援」最有力的宣傳材料，直接促成了1116年至1119年間一批新的西歐援軍開往東方，其中便包括比薩與熱那亞的船隊；1118年的阿斯旺之圍，就是這波援助與鮑德溫自己的遠征計畫結合的結果。國王的聲望因此急升，「勇將國王」的形象確立，耶路撒冷王國在東地中海的戰略地位也隨之上升，並與君士坦丁堡的拜占庭帝國形成拉丁與希臘兩條互相牽制的戰線，十字軍國家第一次在東方站穩了腳跟。對法蒂瑪王朝而言，這是一次聲望與財政上的重創：哈里發本人幾乎被俘，國庫象徵性的軍械與財貨大量落入敵手，維齊爾的威信受損，朝廷被迫放棄新建的都城曼蘇拉而退守開羅。但王朝的實力並未受毀，曼蘇拉與開羅仍在法蒂瑪手中。真正持久的影響在戰略層面：從此法蒂瑪避免與法蘭克人正面決戰，改以水陸封鎖、游擊與掠奪作戰，執行的正是維齊爾在敗後提出的那套消耗辦法。這套「不打正面、只困敵糧」的方針在此後七十多年裡不斷被因襲，最終由薩拉丁發揚光大，導致1187年耶路撒冷的陷落：達魯古城的奇襲雖然一場仗也沒能攻下法蒂瑪的兩座都城，卻是這場延續數代的消耗對抗的起點之一。
impactEn: The battle left deep marks in both the Latin and the Arab worlds. For the Kingdom of Jerusalem, the picture of Baldwin breaking into Egypt with several hundred knights, taking the tents of the Fatimid high command and a great quantity of treasure, struck Europe hard: his letter to the West became the most effective propaganda the kingdom possessed on the need for succour, and it helped set in motion the stream of western reinforcements that reached the East between 1116 and 1119, among them the Pisan and Genoese fleets; the siege of Aswan in 1118 was the product of that wave of aid joined to Baldwin's own plans. The king's prestige rose accordingly, the image of the warrior-king was established, and the kingdom of Jerusalem gained a dominant position in the eastern Mediterranean, opening the Latin and Greek fronts at Constantinople against each other for the first time: the crusader states now stood firm in the East. For the Fatimid dynasty it was a blow to prestige and finances. The caliph very nearly fell into enemy hands, the symbolic wealth of the state's arsenal and treasury was carried off, the vizier's authority was shaken, and the court was forced to abandon the new capital of Mansurah and fall back on Cairo. The dynasty's substance, however, was not destroyed; Mansurah and Cairo remained in Fatimid hands. The durable effect was strategic. From that moment the Fatimids avoided pitched battle with the Franks and fought by water and land interdiction, raiding and denial, following exactly the attritional course the vizier had proposed after his defeat. That doctrine was taken up and refined over the following seventy years, and was eventually perfected by Saladin, who took Jerusalem in 1187. The raid at Dar al-Mansurah, although it did not take a single Fatimid capital, was one of the opening moves of that long contest of exhaustion.
result: 結果要分幾層看。野戰層面是法蘭克人的完勝：鮑德溫在黎明時攻破維齊爾阿夫達勒的營地，奪取哈里發與維齊爾的帳幕、旗幔、軍械與大量財貨，法蒂瑪大軍在夜色中潰散，退回開羅與曼蘇拉城內，統帥的營帳與印璽都成了戰利品。攻城層面則一無所獲：曼蘇拉有護城河與城牆，鮑德溫既無重型攻城器械，兵力也不足以合圍，圍城七日不能下，城守軍出城反擊又逼他解圍；隨後他進軍開羅，開羅外圍與部分城區被放棄，他一度進入城中，但得知上埃及方向的大軍正在逼近，立刻改為撤退，未與法蒂瑪主力再作決戰。撤退時他沿原路穿越西奈沙漠，隊伍因缺水缺糧大量掉隊。戰略層面上，這是一場典型的「戰術上完全勝利、戰略上毫無成果」的戰役：法蒂瑪王朝毫髮無傷地保住了兩座都城與尼羅河航路，但被迫放棄新首都、損失大批軍械財貨與士氣，並因此轉向長期消耗的國策；鮑德溫則收穫了難得的財富、經驗與聲望，確立了他作為勇將國王的地位，也為1118年那次規模更大、配合同盟船隊的遠征鋪了路。就本卡兵器而言，結論同樣清楚：配重投石車這類新式攻城機在達魯古城之戰中完全沒有出現，決定勝負的是渡河、奇襲與撤退時的補給線，而不是任何攻城武器；它在後來對付有護城河與城牆的埃及城市時才會真正登場。
resultEn: The outcome has to be read on several levels. On the field the result was a complete Frankish victory: at dawn Baldwin broke into al-Afdal's camp, took the tents, banners, weapons and a great quantity of treasure of the caliph and his vizier, and the Fatimid host broke up in the dark and fell back into Cairo and the fortified city of Mansurah; the commander's pavilion and the caliph's seal became spoils. At the level of siegecraft the result was nothing at all. Mansurah had its moat and its walls; Baldwin had neither heavy engines to breach them nor the men to invest the place properly, and after seven days, with the garrison sallying out to drive off the besiegers, he had to raise the siege. He then advanced on Cairo, whose outer works and part of the city were abandoned, and he entered the place; but on learning that a large army was approaching from Upper Egypt he turned back immediately without risking a second pitched battle with the Fatimids. On the return he retraced his route across the Sinai with the army straggling badly for want of water and grain. Strategically, then, this was a textbook case of total tactical success and total strategic failure: the Fatimid dynasty lost neither of its two capitals nor the Nile, but it did give up the new capital, the arsenal, the treasury and a good deal of prestige, and it was driven onto a long attritional policy; Baldwin gained hard-won wealth, experience and renown, established himself as a warrior-king, and prepared the ground for the much larger expedition of 1118 with the help of the allied fleets. As for the weapon on the card, the conclusion is equally plain: no counterweight trebuchet appeared at Dar al-Mansurah. What decided the day was the river crossing, the surprise and the supply line on the withdrawal, not any siege engine. The trebuchet's hour would come only later, against the moated and walled Egyptian cities.
